title: fix(app-shell,i18n): marketplace 「更新」 opens an update dialog naming both versions, with a major-version notice and no sample-data box; README raw HTML is skipped, not printed (objectui#12146)
body:
Fixes #12146
Clause-②: yes

Both items of the card, as triage `6110813809` directs. Measured on head `e167808`.

## What changed

**Item 1: the update dialog.** On the marketplace package page, the primary button reads 「更新」 when this environment holds an older version. It used to open the install dialog unchanged. The same dialog component now opens in an update mode. The mode is fixed when the dialog opens (`DialogUpdate` in `MarketplacePackagePage.tsx`), so the update's own success, which flips the installed version, cannot turn the dialog back into an install dialog. In update mode:

- the title is 「更新 HotCRM」 ("Update HotCRM"), the description is "Update the copy installed in this environment (HOST).", and the primary button is 「更新」, with "Updating…" while it runs. The page's own button behind the modal also says "Updating…";
- the dialog names `v3.1.0 → v4.0.1`. Both versions are the ones the page already shows: the installed version and `latestVersion`;
- **a major-version jump** adds one line saying so (`marketplace.update.majorNotice`), with a link to the target version's notes in the side panel's Versions list. Following the link closes the dialog and moves focus and scroll to that entry, through `onCloseAutoFocus`. The link is drawn only when the target version has notes;
- **no 「包含示例数据」 checkbox**, and the update sends `seedSampleData: false`, which is what an unticked checkbox sends today. Sample data for an installed copy stays with the page's own "Add sample data" action;
- **the result** is 「已更新到 v4.0.1」 ("Updated to v4.0.1"). It uses the version the install answer names, or the dialog's target when the answer names none. If the served-wait times out, the dialog says the update was recorded but the new version is not served yet.

The install path renders as before: the same keys, the same checkbox and the same request. The CONTROL pin checks this.

**Item 2: the README's raw HTML.** `MarkdownText` is this console's own CommonMark-subset renderer. It is hand-written, with no markdown engine underneath (see the H3 reading below). It used to read a raw-HTML block as a paragraph and print its tags as text. Its parser now recognises raw HTML by CommonMark's own grammar:

- the seven start and end conditions of the "HTML blocks" section;
- the inline forms of the "Raw HTML" section.

The renderer then skips that HTML, the same way react-markdown's `skipHtml` does. The source is never pre-filtered, so HTML inside a code span or a fenced block is still code and still prints. Text that only looks like a tag stays text: a comparison, or an angle-bracketed URL.

## Readings (the dispatch's mechanism hypotheses)

- **H1, confirmed.** 「更新」 calls the same `openInstall` as the install button and renders the same dialog unchanged: install title, `marketplace.action.install`, the sample-data checkbox, and `marketplace.install.success` or `install.deployed` as the result.
- **H2, measured as far as this session can reach. The ruling's two branches give the same action.** The dialog's install door is `installPackage` (`marketplaceApi.ts`). On a tenant runtime it posts to the same-origin `/api/v1/cloud-connection/install`. objectstack's handler for that route (`packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts` on objectstack `origin/main` `9fdb12752`, the `POST /install` route) reads `seed_sample_data` and **forwards it unchanged** to the control plane's `sys_package/install_package` action. It has no branch of its own for an environment that already holds the package. The control-plane path posts to that same action directly. The branch that decides what the flag does on an existing install is in objectstack-ai/cloud, and this session has no read access to it (`add_repo` answered "you don't have access"). **The cloud half is NOT MEASURED.** The ruling hides the checkbox both if it would seed into live data and if it is a no-op, so the action does not depend on that reading: the update hides it and sends `false`.
- **H3, falsified. Route changed to match the ruling's intent.** `MarkdownText.tsx` is a hand-written subset renderer. It imports no markdown library, so it has no option of its own to drop raw HTML. Two routes were possible: (a) move the README to react-markdown with `skipHtml`, through `@object-ui/fields`' `MarkdownContent`; (b) teach this renderer's parser CommonMark's HTML grammar and skip that node. Route (b) is the one taken. Route (a) leaves the claimed file surface: `MarkdownContent` exposes no `skipHtml` prop. It would also change how every README renders: images, tables and GFM, which this renderer deliberately does not draw. The "no ad-hoc regex" line is kept in the sense the ruling gives it. Nothing strips the source before parsing. HTML is a parser node, recognised by the spec's own start conditions, and the renderer skips it. If the seat prefers (a), it is a separate change on `packages/fields`.
- **H4, confirmed.** Eight keys are added in all ten packs: `marketplace.update.dialogTitle`, `dialogDescCurrent`, `dialogDescPicker`, `majorNotice`, `releaseNotes`, `success` and `deployTimeout`, plus `marketplace.action.updating`. They widen the published `TranslationKeys`, so the claim's `Clause-②: yes` stands. The from-to line reuses `marketplace.versionBadge` and the button reuses `marketplace.action.updateTo`, so neither needs a key of its own.

## Bounded in-place fix, named

Inline raw HTML is dropped as well: `Built by` + a bold-tag pair around `Acme` renders as "Built by Acme". This is the same defect class as the block form (a README's raw HTML printed as text), in the same file and gated by the same pins. Evidence: the pin "drops inline raw HTML and keeps the text between the tags" is green on head and red when `MarkdownText.tsx` is ablated (below).

## Tests

- New `MarketplacePackagePage.updateDialog-12146.test.tsx`: update title, description, versions and button; no checkbox and `seedSampleData: false` in the request; "Updated to v4.0.1" on the served state; a major jump gives the notice and the link, and following the link closes the dialog and focuses the 4.0.1 entry; CONTROL: a minor update draws no notice; CONTROL: a fresh install opens today's dialog, and the checkbox still drives `seedSampleData: true`.
- New `MarkdownText.rawHtml-12146.test.tsx`: the HotCRM-shaped README (the block is neither rendered nor printed, and the markdown after it is intact); the one-line form; every start condition (script, comment, declaration, a block tag, a lone tag); a paragraph interrupted by a block start; inline HTML; CONTROLS: code spans and fences still print, a comparison and an angle-bracketed URL stay text, and a README without HTML renders as before.
- `MarketplacePackagePage.servedTruth-12098.test.tsx` (the objectui#12098 pin): its upgrade path now clicks the update dialog's 「更新」 and reads "Updated to" on the served state. The served-version wait it measures is unchanged.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/` gives `Test Files 31 passed (31)`, `Tests 196 passed (196)`. `pnpm exec vitest run packages/i18n/` gives `Test Files 83 passed (83)`, `Tests 1321 passed | 13 skipped (1334)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` exits 0 on `e167808`. It runs `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, and the test project includes `src/**/*.test.tsx`. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/i18n type-check` exits 0. Both ran after `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2` (28 of 28 tasks, exit 0).

**Ablation.** Each source file was reverted to the base blob and both new pin files were run. The mutation was proven by blob hash, and restored from `HEAD` with an empty `git diff HEAD`:

- `MarkdownText.tsx` at base: the 5 raw-HTML pins are red, and its 3 CONTROLS and all page pins stay green (`5 failed | 8 passed`).
- `MarketplacePackagePage.tsx` at base: the 4 update-mode pins are red. One of them is the minor-update case, which asserts the versions line. The fresh-install CONTROL stays green (`4 failed | 9 passed`).
- A bogus key in a new `t()` call turns `check:i18n-keys` red (`[missing-key] marketplace.update.releaseNotesBogus`). That shows the gate reads these call sites. There is no type-level reverse check to run: `t` is react-i18next's untyped `TFunction` here, and no source outside `packages/i18n` consumes `TranslationKeys` except a re-export in `packages/react`.

## Gates (head `e167808`)

- exit 0: `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift` (0 `en` values changed, 8 keys added), `check:i18n-dead-keys` (report-only; none of the new keys listed), `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:phantom-deps`, `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:eager-locale-catalogues`. Reason: PREREQUISITE NOT MET, because it reads a built console bundle (`apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json`). That needs a console build, which belongs to CI here, and so does the eager-closure budget.
- Lint, a narrowing whose coverage is shown: ESLint on the 15 changed source files, from each package's own directory as its `lint` script (`eslint .`) runs. `--format json` reports 5 files for app-shell and 10 for i18n, 0 errors. The 11 warnings all sit on lines that blame to commits before this branch (`no-explicit-any` and one unused var), and no added line carries `any`. `eslint.config.js` declares no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`, so lint is not type-aware and this diff cannot move a verdict in an untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## File surface

The claim's surface, plus one file outside it: `MarketplacePackagePage.servedTruth-12098.test.tsx`. It pinned the install button's name and the install's "deployed" sentence on the upgrade path, which this card changes on purpose. The edit is the selector and that one expected sentence. No other claim holds it. The surface addition is named here so the seat can record it.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed)

- On a runtime with a cloud base and no `defaultEnvironmentId`, the dialog shows the environment picker, but `installPackage` installs into the environment the hostname names and never reads the pick. This is pre-existing and documented in `installPackage`, and the update mode inherits it unchanged. It was read from source and not reproduced. Carrier: none.
- `MarkdownText` has no indented code blocks, a pre-existing subset limit. A raw tag indented four spaces is therefore read as paragraph text, and its inline HTML is dropped instead of printed as code. Carrier: none.
- The from-version is the page's installed version for this environment. In the picker branch, the picker's per-environment annotations ("Installed vX" / "Update → vY") remain the per-target reading. Carrier: none.
